findings.note: Real-world geology strongly links collapse with sinkhole and dissolution with cenote (cenotes are classically described as dissolution-formed sinkholes), so a player may want to pair collapse:sinkhole and dissolution:cenote instead of the intended collapse:crater and dissolution:chasm, undermining confidence even after solving.

notes:
Cross-set association between set-cause-effect-formation and set-taxonomic-caves lets solvers swap in the real-world dissolution:cenote / collapse:sinkhole pairing instead of the intended collapse:crater / dissolution:chasm, undermining confidence. Fix by replacing the effect words in set-cause-effect-formation with results that aren't classic karst-type nouns overlapping with the taxonomic set's vocabulary.
- set-cause-effect-formation: collapse:crater and dissolution:chasm are real-world confusable with collapse:sinkhole and dissolution:cenote from the taxonomic set, so solvers plausibly swap pairs across sets and distrust their solution.
  Try: Replace 'crater' with a non-karst collapse result such as 'collapse : cave-in' or 'collapse : subsidence' to remove overlap with sinkhole/cenote vocabulary
  Or: Replace 'chasm' with a dissolution-specific but non-sinkhole-adjacent result such as 'dissolution : cavern' (paired with a matching non-karst-typed collapse effect) so neither word reads as a karst subtype
  Or: Change both effect words to results outside the sinkhole/cenote semantic field entirely, e.g. 'collapse : rubble' and 'dissolution : channel', ensuring neither is a taxonomic karst term
Do not change: set-object-component-hollow, set-agent-instrument-explorers, set-taxonomic-caves — no allowlisted finding touches them.

persisted.note: Anyone with basic karst-geology knowledge knows sinkholes and cenotes often form by roof collapse, and caves/grottoes form by dissolution — so a player could easily want to pair collapse:sinkhole or dissolution:cave instead of the intended collapse:rubble / dissolution:channel, since the taxonomic set's nouns are the real-world products of the cause-effect set's processes.
